name: create a virtual environment

examples.note: convention: name it .venv in the project root

gotchas: activate only changes the CURRENT shell; new terminals must re-activate
once active, use plain 'python'/'pip' — they point inside the venv
explanation: A venv isolates dependencies per project so installs don't pollute the system Python.

name: install a package (the safe way)
description: install with pip via -m so it targets the interpreter you ran

examples.note: goes into the active venv, or use --user outside one
quote version specifiers so the shell doesn't parse < >

gotchas: prefer 'python -m pip' over a bare 'pip' so you KNOW which interpreter gets the package

name: install from a requirements file
description: install every pinned dependency listed in the file

examples.note: snapshot the CURRENT env's exact versions

gotchas: pip freeze captures everything installed incl. transitive deps; for clean top-level deps use a tool like pip-tools or pyproject.toml

name: serve the current directory over HTTP
description: zero-config static file server for the cwd

examples.note: -b bind address (localhost-only), -d serve a different dir

gotchas: it serves to anything that can reach the port; bind 127.0.0.1 if you don't want it on the LAN

name: pretty-print / validate JSON
description: reformat JSON with indentation (and validate it)

examples.note: pipe an API response through it

gotchas: key order is PRESERVED by default — pass --sort-keys if you want them alphabetised

name: debug with pdb
description: run a script under the built-in debugger

examples.note: starts paused; n=next, s=step in, c=continue, p <expr>=print, l=list, q=quit
drop this line in your code to halt there (Python 3.7+)

explanation: breakpoint() honours $PYTHONBREAKPOINT — set it to 0 to disable all breakpoints, or to ipdb.set_trace for a richer debugger.

name: run a one-liner
description: execute Python from the command line without a file
gotchas: you can't have a top-level indented block on one line; use ; for simple statements or pipe a heredoc to python3 -

name: micro-benchmark a snippet
description: time a small statement, auto-choosing the loop count

examples.cmd: python3 -m timeit '"-".join(str(n) for n in range(100))'

name: inspect an installed package
description: show version, location, and dependencies of a package

examples.note: which installed packages have newer releases

name: merge two dicts
description: combine dicts; right-hand keys win on conflict (Python 3.9+)
gotchas: on key collision the LATER/right operand wins

name: list / dict / set comprehension
description: build a collection inline with an optional filter

examples.cmd: {k: v for k, v in pairs if v}
examples.note: dict comp with a truthiness filter

gotchas: a comprehension with no key:value but braces, e.g. {x for x in xs}, is a SET, not a dict

command: for i, x in enumerate(<it>, start=1):
name: index while iterating
description: loop with a running counter instead of manual indexing
explanation: Cleaner and faster than 'for i in range(len(xs)): x = xs[i]'. Pair with zip() to walk two sequences together.

name: read a file safely
description: open a file in a context manager so it always closes

examples.cmd: with open('data.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:\n    text = f.read()
examples.note: always pass encoding; the default is platform-dependent
iterate lazily — doesn't load the whole file into memory

gotchas: set encoding='utf-8' explicitly; relying on the locale default bites you on other machines/Windows

name: script-vs-import guard
description: run code only when the file is executed directly, not imported
explanation: __name__ is '__main__' when run as a script, but the module's name when imported — so the guarded code is skipped on import.

command: python3 -m pip install pipx; pipx install <tool>
name: install CLI tools in isolation
description: install Python-based command-line tools without polluting any project

examples.note: each tool gets its own private venv but lands on PATH
run a tool once without installing it

explanation: Use pip+venv for libraries you import; use pipx for applications you run (black, ruff, httpie, poetry).

name: run with dev/warning checks
description: enable extra runtime checks and surface warnings hidden by default

examples.note: shows DeprecationWarnings and enables extra checks
turn warnings into exceptions to find their source
